site.name: IbexWall
home.title: IbexWall: the security center for Linux
home.description: See how secure your Linux computer is, learn what to fix in plain words, and apply each fix as a plan you review and can undo. Free, open source, no telemetry.
hero.title: Know how secure your Linux computer is. Fix it with changes you can undo.
hero.sub: IbexWall checks your system, explains what to improve in plain words, and applies each change only after you have reviewed it. It is free, open source, and it never phones home.
hero.note: Version 1.0 is in preparation. Follow the project on GitHub.
promises.title: Three promises
promise.review.title: Review first
promise.review.text: Every change starts as a plan: the exact files, firewall rules and services it touches, and what could break. Nothing is applied until you say so.
promise.undo.title: Undo any time
promise.undo.text: A snapshot is taken before each change. History shows what changed and puts it back. A change that could cut your network undoes itself unless you confirm.
promise.private.title: Nothing leaves your computer
promise.private.text: No telemetry, no account, no analytics. IbexWall talks to the network only when you ask it to.
features.title: What it does
feature.score.title: A score you can read
feature.score.text: Checks for disk encryption, Secure Boot, the firewall, open ports, updates, SSH and more, each with a plain explanation of what it means and what to do.
feature.hardening.title: Hardening, one tick at a time
feature.hardening.text: 26 kernel, network, file system and module settings, each explained with what it protects and what it can break. Tick the ones you want and apply them in one plan.
feature.firewall.title: A firewall and per-program control
feature.firewall.text: Close what should not listen, and decide which programs may reach the network. IbexWall asks the first time a new program connects.
feature.dns.title: Encrypted DNS
feature.dns.text: Lookups leave your computer encrypted, with tracker and malware blocking. If you already run dnscrypt-proxy, IbexWall recognises it and leaves it alone.
feature.ai.title: Connect an AI assistant safely
feature.ai.text: Let an assistant read your status and suggest changes. It can never apply one: you review every proposal.
feature.plugins.title: Plugins with visible permissions
feature.plugins.text: Thirty-two signed plugins, each in its own sandbox. You can see what each one reads and what it may change.
how.title: How it works
how.1.title: Check
how.1.text: IbexWall reads your system. It changes nothing while it looks.
how.2.title: Plan
how.2.text: Pick a fix. You see the files, rules and services it would touch, and what could break.
how.3.title: Apply
how.3.text: A snapshot is taken, the change is made, and risky ones wait for your confirmation.
how.4.title: Undo
how.4.text: History puts back exactly what was there before, whenever you want.
trust.title: Built to be trusted
trust.open.title: Open source
trust.open.text: GPL-3.0-or-later. Read it, build it, change it.
trust.signed.title: Signed and traceable
trust.signed.text: Releases carry checksums, signatures, a bill of materials and a provenance statement, and the build can be reproduced.
trust.tested.title: Tested where you run it
trust.tested.text: Fedora, Ubuntu, Debian and Arch, each in a virtual machine for every release.
trust.confined.title: Confined
trust.confined.text: AppArmor profiles and an SELinux module keep the resolver, the assistant server and the plugins to what they need.
trust.languages.title: Your language
trust.languages.text: English, Portuguese, Spanish, French and German, following your system language.
hardening.teaser.title: Every setting, explained
hardening.teaser.text: One page for each hardening setting: why it matters, how it works, who should use it, what you may notice, and how to apply it by hand or with IbexWall.
compliance.title: Compliance, not certification
compliance.description: Which technical controls each framework requires, which this machine meets, and what a local program cannot decide. Compliance means the mapped controls hold, never a certification.
compliance.intro: IbexWall maps each framework to the checks the product already runs, then reports which controls hold, which do not, and which need a person. This is evidence, never a certification.
compliance.disclaimer: Compliance means the mapped technical controls hold on this machine, never a certification. Certification comes from an independent audit, which also covers processes, people and scope that no local program can see.
compliance.limits: What this profile does not claim
articles.teaser.title: Guides
faq.title: Questions
faq.1.a: No. There is no telemetry, account or analytics. The program only uses the network when you ask it to, for example for a DNS lookup you make or a package update you run.
faq.2.a: Every change is a plan you review, with a snapshot taken first and an undo in History. Changes that could cut your network wait for your confirmation and undo themselves if you do not give it.
faq.3.a: Fedora, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Debian and Arch Linux. Each release is tested in virtual machines on all of them.
faq.4.a: No. If you use ufw or firewalld, IbexWall works through it. It keeps to its own rules and files and never edits the ones your distribution or another program owns.
faq.5.a: Yes. It is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later license.
footer.text: IbexWall is free software, GPL-3.0-or-later. No telemetry.
hardening.title: Hardening settings, explained
hardening.description: Twenty-six Linux hardening settings for the kernel, network, file systems and modules: why each one matters, how it works, what it can break, and how to apply it.
hardening.intro: Each page explains one setting in plain words, tells you what you may notice after turning it on, and shows the commands to check and apply it by hand. IbexWall applies the same setting as a plan you review, with a snapshot and an undo.
risk.label: What it can break
risk.explain: How likely it is to affect programs you use
hp.ibex.text: Open Hardening in IbexWall, tick this setting and review the plan. IbexWall writes only its own file, takes a snapshot first, and History undoes it. Nothing is applied until you approve.

hp.sysctl.persist: Keep it after restarts, in a file you own:
hp.sysctl.undo: Remove the file and restart, or set the old value back with sysctl -w.

hp.modules.apply: Tell the system not to load them, in a file you own:
hp.modules.undo: Remove the file. Modules already loaded stay until the next restart.

hp.mount.apply: Add the option to the mount in /etc/fstab, or in a systemd mount unit, then remount:
hp.mount.undo: Take the option out again and remount.
hp.atleast: A stricter value than this one is also fine.
articles.title: Linux security guides
articles.description: Plain-language guides to checking and improving the security of a Linux desktop: firewalls, DNS, Secure Boot, disk encryption, kernel hardening and more.
article.cta.title: Check this on your computer
article.cta.text: IbexWall can run these checks and apply the fixes as plans you review and can undo.
